01 · The Opportunity

The Opportunity

Generative AI is rapidly changing how digital products are imagined, designed, and built.

How might AI accelerate creative exploration while allowing human-centered design to guide product strategy, usability, and brand coherence?

To investigate this, I created BU Super League 2026—a concept platform for an internal sports championship that brought employees together across regions and business units.

Rather than designing another corporate portal, I wanted to create an experience that felt high-energy, community-driven, and emotionally engaging.

The project became an experiment in designing not only a product, but a new design workflow—one where generative AI acts as a creative collaborator, accelerating ideation while human design judgment shapes the user journey, interaction architecture, and design system.

View Interactive Prototype ↗
02 · The Challenge

The Challenge

Employee engagement initiatives often struggle to sustain excitement. Many internal platforms prioritize administration over experience—focusing heavily on logistics while missing the emotional spark that inspires participation.

The challenge was twofold: • First, how could an internal sports championship feel emotionally compelling, identity-driven, and memorable? • Second, how could AI become a creative collaborator during product design—helping generate concepts, interface elements, and brand identities without compromising usability, consistency, or human-centered UX principles?

03 · Design Vision

Design Vision

Instead of designing an event management portal, I envisioned a platform that felt closer to joining a professional sports league.

The experience needed to create anticipation, celebrate identity, and encourage participation before, during, and after each event.

The goal wasn't simply helping employees register. It was helping them feel like they belonged.

04 · My Role & Framing

My Role & Framing

My Role

This was a self-initiated concept project where I led the end-to-end product vision. My responsibilities included:

  • Product strategy
  • UX strategy
  • Information architecture
  • Interaction design
  • Design system direction
  • AI prompt engineering
  • High-fidelity visual exploration
  • Product storytelling

While usability testing was outside the scope of this concept, every design decision was grounded in established UX principles rather than purely visual exploration.

Framing the Design Challenge

Before generating a single screen, I defined the emotional experience I wanted employees to have.

“What should employees feel throughout the journey?”

The desired progression became: Discover the championship → Register effortlessly → Choose preferred sports → Select skill level → Be assigned to a team → Celebrate team identity → Compete with colleagues → Share achievements → Return for future events.

This shifted the experience from completing another HR process to becoming part of a shared organizational culture.

05 · Exploring AI as a Design Partner

Exploring AI as a Design Partner

Instead of asking AI to generate random interfaces, I approached it as a collaborative design tool. Every prompt included strategic direction rather than purely visual requests. The guidance covered:

  • Brand personality
  • Team identities
  • User journeys
  • Interaction behaviors
  • Motion principles
  • Responsive layouts
  • Design system foundations
  • Content hierarchy

This allowed AI to accelerate visual exploration while leaving critical product decisions in the hands of the designer.

What AI Accelerated

The experiment demonstrated several areas where AI significantly improved the design process:

• Rapid concept exploration: Multiple visual directions could be explored within hours instead of days.

• Brand expression & Creative momentum: AI quickly generated distinct visual identities for teams, environments, and interface themes. Rather than beginning with a blank canvas, AI provided starting points that encouraged further refinement.

• Visual consistency: Shared prompts helped maintain a coherent design language across multiple screens.

06 · Where Human Design Was Essential

Where Human Design Was Essential

Perhaps the most valuable outcome wasn't what AI created—it was identifying where human judgment remained irreplaceable.

UX decisions still required careful consideration around:

  • Information hierarchy
  • Accessibility
  • Interaction behavior
  • Progressive disclosure
  • Product strategy
  • User psychology
  • Enterprise feasibility
  • Design trade-offs

The project reinforced that while AI can generate interfaces, it cannot replace the reasoning behind meaningful user experiences.

07 · Experience Highlights & Design Principles

Experience Highlights & Design Principles

Creating emotional moments

One of the core objectives was transforming ordinary product interactions into memorable experiences. Instead of confirming registration with a standard success message, employees are welcomed through a cinematic house assignment sequence featuring animated emblems, dynamic lighting, celebration effects, and personalized messaging.

This interaction was intentionally designed to strengthen emotional investment before the competition even begins.

Extending engagement beyond the event

Many internal sports initiatives lose momentum once matches conclude. To encourage ongoing participation, I designed the Experience Wall—a social space where employees could share match highlights, celebrate victories, post photos, react to teammates, and revisit memorable moments. This transformed the platform from a scheduling tool into a community-building experience.

Design Principles

  • Design for emotion: Memorable experiences create stronger engagement than efficient workflows alone.
  • Identity drives participation: People are more likely to contribute when they feel part of something larger than themselves.
  • AI supports creativity—not decisions: Artificial intelligence accelerates exploration, but product strategy and user experience remain human responsibilities.
  • Systems create consistency: A scalable design system enables innovation without sacrificing usability.
08 · Design System

Design System

The visual language intentionally blended modern sports branding with enterprise usability. Key decisions included:

  • Dark interface optimized for immersive experiences.
  • Bold athletic-inspired typography.
  • Glassmorphism-inspired containers.
  • Dynamic gradients.
  • Animated leaderboard components.
  • Responsive layouts across desktop and mobile.
  • Reusable component library supporting future expansion.

Every visual decision aimed to reinforce excitement while preserving clarity and usability.

09 · Outcomes

Outcomes

Product Outcomes

  • Demonstrated how employee engagement platforms can evolve beyond administrative tools.
  • Explored role-based experiences through immersive interaction design.
  • Established a scalable design system supporting future expansion.

Design Outcomes

  • Developed an effective workflow combining AI-assisted exploration with traditional UX practices.
  • Identified opportunities where AI accelerates creativity without replacing design thinking.
  • Strengthened systems thinking through reusable interaction patterns and visual consistency.

Personal Growth

This project expanded my understanding of how emerging technologies can complement—not compete with—human-centered design. It reinforced the importance of balancing innovation with critical thinking, ensuring that new tools enhance the design process without diminishing the designer's role.

10 · Reflection

Reflection

BU Super League fundamentally changed how I think about AI in design. Rather than viewing AI as a shortcut for generating interfaces, I began seeing it as a creative collaborator capable of accelerating exploration while leaving strategy, empathy, and decision-making firmly in human hands.

More importantly, the project reminded me that meaningful products are rarely defined by their visuals alone. They're defined by the experiences they create, the emotions they evoke, and the communities they help build.

If I were to continue evolving this concept, I would validate the experience through usability testing, measure engagement across different interaction patterns, and explore how AI could support personalized recommendations without compromising transparency or user trust.
